claims.statement: github_webhook_exporter is a single-instance Rust service that authenticates GitHub webhook deliveries per repository, exports bounded-cardinality Prometheus metrics, tracks merge-queue attempts, and projects completed workflow jobs into OTLP traces without persisting payloads, as specified in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-github-webhook-exporter-design.md and README.md.

evidence.summary: All six area parents (CLM-0002..CLM-0007) are refuted. Across 201 leaves: 181 supported, 17 refuted, 3 not_enough_info. Security-relevant refutations: CLM-0195 (IL4, OTLP client follows redirects with custom auth headers), CLM-0037 (IL3, branch path traversal in GitHub API URLs), CLM-0058 (IL3, weak/duplicate admin token accepted); plus clippy -D warnings failure (CLM-0097), CI coverage gaps (CLM-0121, CLM-0132) and doc drift.

verdicts.rationale: The core design holds (authenticated ingestion, bounded metrics, merge-queue tracking, OTLP projection, hardened chart), but every area parent has at least one refuted leaf, three of them security findings. Fix: disable redirects on the OTLP exporter HTTP client in src/telemetry.rs build_blocking_http_client and add a 307 regression test, then re-audit the remaining refuted leaves.

claims.statement: Spec 01 (service and repository configuration) holds: runtime configuration, the authenticated repository configuration API, encrypted repository secrets, SQLite repository store, health endpoints and graceful lifecycle behave as specified.

evidence.summary: 35 leaves: 32 supported, 3 refuted. Refuted: CLM-0058 (IL3, admin token entropy/independence from master key not enforced; 1-char token and token equal to master key both start), CLM-0051 (IL1, spec says secret types never implement Debug but they implement redacted Debug), CLM-0073 (IL1, build-spec example still shows Bearer <master-key>).

verdicts.rationale: Three child leaves are refuted, including one IL3 security leaf: the admin token is not checked for entropy or independence from the master key. Fix: reject GHE_ADMIN_TOKEN values shorter than 32 characters or equal to the encoded master key at startup, and correct the two spec/build-spec wording errors.

claims.statement: Spec 02 (webhook ingestion and metrics) holds: webhook authentication, delivery deduplication, retention, and bounded-cardinality Prometheus metrics behave as specified.

evidence.summary: 33 leaves: 30 supported, 3 refuted. All IL3-4 ingestion security leaves (2 MiB limit, exact-byte constant-time HMAC, content type, allowlisted labels, atomic dedup) supported. Refuted: CLM-0168 (IL2, two warn! calls in src/api/webhook.rs log repository names and delivery IDs against spec 02 logging rule), CLM-0169 (IL1, build-spec failure-stage list stale), CLM-0170 (IL1, build-spec links non-existent README#metrics).

verdicts.rationale: Core ingestion security holds, but three child leaves are refuted: trace-rejection warnings log repository names and delivery IDs contrary to spec 02, and two build-spec passages are stale. Fix: either drop repository and delivery ID from the two warn! calls in src/api/webhook.rs or amend the spec 02 logging rule, then update the build-spec failure-stage list and metrics link.

claims.statement: Spec 03 (merge-queue tracking) holds: merge_group and pull_request events drive durable merge-queue attempt state, outcomes and durations as specified, including required-check handling and GitHub API refresh.

evidence.summary: 31 leaves: 28 supported, 2 refuted, 1 not_enough_info. Refuted: CLM-0037 (IL3 security, webhook branch names with '..' segments are not rejected and the encode set leaves '/' and '.' literal, so the GitHub API URL carrying the installation token can normalize to a different path), CLM-0038 (IL1, build-spec dequeue classifier description stale). NEI: CLM-0031 (client timeout and 256 KiB cap untested; body fully buffered before the cap is checked).

verdicts.rationale: The attempt state machine, durability and metric bounds hold, but an IL3 security leaf is refuted (branch path traversal in GitHub API URLs) and one doc leaf is stale. Fix: reject branch names containing '.' or '..' path segments before building GitHub API URLs in src/github/client.rs, with a regression test.

claims.statement: Spec 04 (OTLP observability) and the later tracing specs hold: validated, bounded OTLP export of service and workflow-job traces, workflow span context, exception events and failure diagnostics behave as specified.

evidence.summary: 38 leaves: 36 supported, 2 refuted. Refuted: CLM-0195 (IL4 security, build_blocking_http_client at src/telemetry.rs:691 sets no redirect policy, so reqwest follows redirects and forwards custom OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS such as API keys cross-host; coordinator confirmed the builder has only .timeout()), CLM-0194 (IL2, OTLP spec 04 forbids repo/PR/SHA/delivery attributes on spans that later specs and code deliberately emit).

verdicts.rationale: Bounded, validated OTLP export holds, but an IL4 security leaf is refuted: the exporter HTTP client follows redirects and can forward custom OTLP auth headers to another host. Fix: add .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none()) in build_blocking_http_client (src/telemetry.rs) with a local 307 regression test, and amend the spec 04 Spans section.

claims.statement: Spec 05 (Kubernetes packaging) and the later container, Helm, CI and release specs hold: the hardened image, singleton StatefulSet Helm chart, network boundaries, CI policy, backup/recovery and release publication behave as specified.

evidence.summary: 36 leaves: 32 supported, 2 refuted, 2 not_enough_info. claims.statement: The merge_queue_attempts migration enforces outcome IN (pending,succeeded,failed,cancelled,unknown), pull_request_number > 0, and the pending<->completed_at NULL check, and creates the one_active partial unique index and completed_at index exactly as specified.

All 10 tests in merge_queue_storage pass, including the schema test that exercises the constraints against a migrated database.

verdicts.rationale: Migration text matches the spec and the schema test passes against a migrated DB.

claims.statement: At most one active (completed_at IS NULL) attempt exists per (repository_id, pull_request_number) even under concurrent enqueue calls.
claims.source: spec 03 State transitions: Concurrent transitions serialize ... partial unique index

evidence.summary: Test passes: concurrent enqueues leave exactly one active row.

enqueue uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(repository_id, pull_request_number) WHERE completed_at IS NULL DO NOTHING in one transaction, relying on the partial unique index; rows_affected distinguishes Created vs AlreadyActive.

verdicts.rationale: Concurrent test passes and the INSERT relies on the partial unique index with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

claims.statement: An enqueued event while an active attempt exists is idempotent: it changes no persisted state and records no outcome metric.

evidence.locator: cargo test --test merge_queue_storage sequential_transitions_are_exact_and_idempotent (tests/merge_queue_storage.rs:252-290); cargo test --test webhook_api pull_request_queue_replays_and_unmerged_close_are_idempotent
evidence.summary: Both pass. Repeated enqueue returns AlreadyActive and the row keeps the first enqueued_at, pending/none; the webhook test shows a second enqueue leaves one attempt and no outcome metric change.
AlreadyActive maps to OperationOutcome::NoOp and no metrics method is called on the enqueue path at all.

verdicts.rationale: Tests show unchanged row and metrics on repeated enqueue; code path records no metric.

claims.statement: A pull_request.dequeued event completes the active attempt as outcome 'unknown' with reason_code 'unclassified_dequeue', and the raw dequeue reason is never read, persisted, logged or used as a label.
claims.source: spec 03 State transitions + V1 deliberately does not guess

evidence.summary: Passes. Fixture PULL_REQUEST_DEQUEUED carries reason \"malicious-raw-reason\"; row ends outcome=unknown, reason_code=unclassified_dequeue and the exposition does not contain the raw reason (line 357).

PullRequestProjection has no reason field; the top-level `reason` in EventProjection is read only inside merge_group_transition (Destroyed of a merge_group event). The pull-request path never touches it, so the raw dequeue reason is never stored, logged or labeled. Test at webhook_api.rs:686 also asserts it is absent from response, metrics and logs on the failure path.

verdicts.rationale: Test with a hostile raw reason ends unknown/unclassified_dequeue with no leakage; the pull_request projection has no reason field so it cannot be read.

claims.statement: pull_request.closed with merged == true completes the active attempt as 'succeeded' with reason 'pull_request_merged'; closed with merged false or absent changes nothing.

evidence.summary: Passes: enqueue, closed merged:false (no change), then merged closes yield one attempt, outcome=succeeded, reason=pull_request_merged.
Action::Closed maps to a Complete transition only when projection.merged == Some(true); other values fall to the exhaustive None arm.

verdicts.rationale: Test and the merged == Some(true) guard demonstrate both the success and the unmerged no-op cases.

claims.statement: A completion event with no active and no completed attempt changes no persisted state and increments transition_failures with reason missing_active_attempt, without touching outcome metrics.

evidence.locator: cargo test --test webhook_api pull_request_queue_missing_and_invalid_duration_use_only_failure_metrics (tests/webhook_api.rs:568); tests/merge_queue_storage.rs:~355 complete on pr 404
evidence.summary: Passes: dequeue with no attempt gives 204, transition_failures{reason=missing_active_attempt}=1, outcome counter for owner/repository absent; store test returns MissingActiveAttempt for PR 404.
When UPDATE ... RETURNING yields no row and no completed row exists, MissingActiveAttempt is returned with no write; the caller records only the transition-failure metric.

verdicts.rationale: Webhook and store tests plus code show no write and only the missing_active_attempt failure counter.

claims.statement: A completion for an already completed attempt is a no-op: the stored outcome/completed_at are unchanged and no outcome or duration metric is recorded.

evidence.locator: cargo test --test merge_queue_storage sequential_transitions_are_exact_and_idempotent; cargo test --test webhook_api pull_request_queue_replays_and_unmerged_close_are_idempotent
evidence.summary: Store test: second complete on a completed attempt returns AlreadyCompleted and row keeps first completed_at/outcome. Webhook test: repeated merged-close deliveries leave attempt_count 1 and outcome counters at 1.
UPDATE is guarded by completed_at IS NULL so completed rows are never rewritten; AlreadyCompleted maps to NoOp without metrics.

verdicts.rationale: UPDATE guarded by completed_at IS NULL; tests show AlreadyCompleted and unchanged counters.

claims.statement: Concurrent completions of the same attempt apply exactly one terminal transition and record exactly one outcome metric.

evidence.locator: cargo test --test merge_queue_storage concurrent_completions_apply_exactly_one_terminal_transition; cargo test --test webhook_api concurrent_pull_request_queue_completions_record_one_outcome
evidence.summary: Both pass: one Completed among concurrent completers, others AlreadyCompleted; webhook-level concurrent deliveries yield outcome counter exactly 1.

verdicts.rationale: Store-level and webhook-level concurrency tests both pass with exactly one transition and one metric.

claims.statement: A pending attempt persisted before the SQLite database is closed and reopened can be completed afterwards, with its original enqueued_at used for the duration.
claims.source: spec 03 Tests: Restart tests; Acceptance criteria 1

evidence.locator: cargo test --test merge_queue_storage pending_attempt_survives_reopen_and_completes_later (tests/merge_queue_storage.rs:463); cargo test --test webhook_api pull_request_queue_attempt_completes_after_database_restart (tests/webhook_api.rs:413)
evidence.summary: Both pass: the pool is closed, the database reopened via open_database, and completion returns Completed with the original enqueued_at (store test) and the webhook path records attempt succeeded and duration count 1 (webhook test). Webhook test asserts duration count not the sum value.

verdicts.rationale: Pool closed and database reopened in both tests; pending attempt completes with its original enqueued_at.

claims.statement: If the queue transaction fails, the attempt row stays unchanged and no outcome metric is recorded (rollback leaves attempts and outcome metrics unchanged).

evidence.locator: cargo test --test merge_queue_storage failed_completion_rolls_back_the_pending_attempt (tests/merge_queue_storage.rs:499); cargo test --test webhook_api pull_request_queue_state_failure_is_redacted_observable_and_returns_no_content
evidence.summary: Both pass: an aborting trigger causes Internal error, the row stays pending/none/completed_at NULL, and the exposition shows outcome counter 0 for the failed dequeue.
complete_inner commits the transaction only on success; metrics are recorded by the caller only after store.complete returned Ok(Completed), so an error short-circuits via `?` before any metric call.

verdicts.rationale: Forced failure leaves row pending and outcome counter 0; metrics are recorded only after a successful commit.

claims.statement: The queue event timestamp is the validated RFC 3339 pull_request.updated_at normalized to UTC milliseconds; receipt time is used when it is absent or invalid.

evidence.locator: cargo test --test webhook_api pull_request_queue_uses_receipt_fallback_and_rejects_malformed_typed_projection (tests/webhook_api.rs:531); cargo test --test merge_queue_storage queue_domain_values_are_validated_and_bounded
evidence.summary: Both pass: malformed updated_at falls back to receipt time within the request window; QueueTimestamp::parse validates RFC 3339 and canonicalizes to UTC ms.

parse(updated_at).ok().or_else(from_datetime(received_at)); canonical format is [year]-[month]-[day]T..[subsecond digits:3]Z in UTC. Observation: a future-dated but valid updated_at is accepted as-is (no clamp to receipt time); this is spec-compliant and later surfaces as invalid_duration.

verdicts.rationale: Parse/normalize and receipt fallback are implemented and tested.

claims.statement: Attempt durations below zero or above 365 days are not observed: they increment only transition_failures{reason=invalid_duration} and leave the outcome counter and duration histogram untouched; 0 and exactly 365 days are accepted.
claims.source: spec 03 Metrics: Negative or unreasonably large durations are omitted

evidence.summary: Pass: -1ns and 365d+1ns increment invalid_duration (2) with outcome counter and histogram count staying 0; exactly 365d is accepted; webhook-level future enqueue followed by past dequeue yields invalid_duration=1.

Range check (ZERO..=365d).contains(&duration) precedes any outcome or histogram update; invalid values return early after the failure counter. Note the DB attempt is already committed as completed in that case (intended: durations are omitted, state is not).

verdicts.rationale: Boundary tests at -1ns, 365d and 365d+1ns plus the early-return code confirm the bounds.

claims.statement: The recorded duration equals the completion event timestamp minus the persisted enqueued_at (read from the same transaction that completed the row), so measurement survives restarts and does not depend on in-process state.

evidence.summary: UPDATE ... RETURNING enqueued_at inside the completing transaction yields the persisted value, parsed to QueueTimestamp; duration = completion.completed_at().duration_since(&enqueued_at) using event timestamps, not process clock.

Store test asserts Completed{enqueued_at} equals the persisted enqueue timestamp; metrics test asserts a 90s duration yields _sum 90.0. No single end-to-end test asserts the histogram sum from two webhook timestamps, so the composition is covered by two tests plus code reading.

verdicts.rationale: Code computes the duration from the persisted enqueue time returned by the completing transaction; component tests cover each half, though no single test asserts the end-to-end sum.

claims.statement: The attempt-duration histogram uses a fixed 15-bucket layout from 1s to 365 days, so series count per (repository,outcome) is constant and the upper bucket equals the validity ceiling.

evidence.summary: MERGE_QUEUE_ATTEMPT_DURATION_BUCKETS is a const [f64;15] from 1s to 31,536,000s (365d), equal to MAX_MERGE_QUEUE_ATTEMPT_DURATION; histogram constructor uses exactly these buckets. Test long_queue_durations_retain_finite_histogram_resolution passes showing 30d lands in finite buckets.

verdicts.rationale: Const array of 15 buckets ends at 31,536,000s equal to the 365 day ceiling.

claims.statement: Merge-group destroyed reasons map by exact, case-sensitive match to merged/dequeued/invalidated; every other raw value (absent, non-string, unknown) maps to 'other', and checks_requested has reason 'none'.

evidence.summary: Both pass: exact-match mapping; absent, non-string, differently cased and malicious reasons collapse to 'other' with no disclosure in metrics.
normalize_merge_group_destroyed_reason matches only exact "merged"/"dequeued"/"invalidated"; ChecksRequested pairs with MergeGroupReason::None; missing/non-string uses Other.

verdicts.rationale: Exact-match function and tests with untrusted reasons confirm the closed mapping.

claims.statement: merge_group events update github_merge_group_events_total only and never create or complete pull-request merge_queue_attempts rows.
claims.source: spec 03 Merge-group classification: Group events do not mutate pull-request attempts

evidence.summary: Passes: checks_requested and destroyed deliveries increment group counters; the test name and assertions confirm no merge_queue_attempts rows are created.

The merge-group branch calls only metrics.record_merge_group_event and span helpers; QueueProcessor is built solely from event_projection.pull_request(), and process() returns early unless event_type == PullRequest, so merge_group payloads cannot reach MergeQueueStore.

verdicts.rationale: The merge_group handler touches only metrics and spans, and the queue processor is gated on event type pull_request.

claims.statement: The queue metric labels are bounded: repository is the authenticated canonical lowercase name, and action/reason/outcome come from closed Rust enums; no raw reason, PR number, SHA or delivery id can reach a label.

evidence.summary: Queue label sets are typed structs: repository via RepositoryLabel::authenticated(&CanonicalRepositoryName), outcome/reason/action/failure reason are closed enums with fixed as_str; MergeQueueCompletion fixes the outcome/reason pairing. No string-typed raw field exists in any queue label struct; startup seeds only fixed combinations.
Pass: malicious raw reasons, payload fragments, SHA and delivery ids absent from /metrics output.

verdicts.rationale: Typed label structs use closed enums and the authenticated repository newtype; tests with hostile input show no leakage.

claims.statement: A queue-state transaction failure still returns 204, increments github_webhook_processing_failures_total{stage=queue_state}, and emits only a redacted error log (no repository name, delivery id, SQL error text).

evidence.summary: Passes: with an aborting trigger the response is 204, processing_failures{stage=queue_state}=1, exactly one 'GitHub webhook processing failed' log with error_correlation_id, and response/metrics/logs contain no repository name, delivery id, secret, SHA or SQL error text.

process() Err is swallowed into record_queue_state_failure (metric + redacted error! log) and the handler still returns Ok(Success) leading to 204. MergeQueueStoreError Debug/Display are fixed strings.

verdicts.rationale: Test with injected DB failure shows 204, the queue_state counter, and redacted single log line.

claims.statement: Queue processing runs only after webhook authentication and delivery claiming; a duplicate delivery id does not re-run queue transitions or repeat event metrics.

evidence.locator: cargo test --test webhook_api duplicate_merge_group_delivery_does_not_repeat_event_metrics; pull_request_queue_state_failure_is_redacted_observable_and_returns_no_content (replay of claimed delivery)
evidence.summary: Pass: duplicate merge_group delivery does not repeat metrics; replay of a claimed delivery after a queue failure is counted as duplicate and does not retry the transition.
Queue code sits inside the Ok arm of the delivery-claim match; claim Err yields unavailable_error before any queue work. Authentication precedes this handler stage.

verdicts.rationale: Queue code is nested in the successful-claim arm and duplicate tests confirm no repeat.

claims.statement: The 'failed' and 'cancelled' outcomes cannot be produced by any code path in v1: QueueCompletion exposes only pull_request_merged and unclassified_dequeue constructors.

evidence.summary: QueueCompletion fields are private with only pull_request_merged() and unclassified_dequeue() constructors; the store's complete() accepts only &QueueCompletion; the metrics MergeQueueCompletion enum has only two variants. Failed/Cancelled variants exist in the enum but are unconstructible by any completion path.

verdicts.rationale: Private fields and only two constructors make failed/cancelled unreachable.

claims.statement: Completed-attempt retention defaults to 90 days, is configurable via GHE_MERGE_QUEUE_RETENTION_DAYS, and rejects zero, non-numeric and overflowing values.

evidence.summary: DEFAULT_MERGE_QUEUE_RETENTION_DAYS=90; test asserts default Duration 90*86400s; invalid cases 0, not-a-number and u64::MAX are asserted to be rejected for GHE_MERGE_QUEUE_RETENTION_DAYS.

verdicts.rationale: Default and rejection cases are asserted by config tests.

claims.statement: Pruning deletes at most 1000 rows per batch, only completed attempts with completed_at older than the cutoff, and never pending attempts; the scheduled retention pass includes the queue store.

evidence.summary: DELETE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL AND completed_at < ? ORDER BY completed_at, id LIMIT ?) with LIMIT 1000; pending rows (NULL completed_at) cannot match. Note: pending attempts with a missed dequeue are never pruned, so a lost terminal event leaves an orphan row indefinitely (spec silent).

evidence.locator: cargo test --test merge_queue_storage prune_completed_batch_is_bounded_and_preserves_pending_and_fresh_attempts (tests/merge_queue_storage.rs:574); cargo test --lib retention::tests
evidence.summary: Pass: batch deletes are capped at 1000, then remainder, only old completed rows removed (retained 2001, 2002 pending/fresh); retention tests show queue pruning in the scheduled pass, including after a delivery-store failure.

verdicts.rationale: Test and SQL show a 1000 row cap, completed-only deletion, and inclusion in the scheduled pass.

claims.statement: Deleting a repository row cascades to delete its merge_queue_attempts.

evidence.summary: Passes: deleting the repository removes its pending and completed attempts (FK ON DELETE CASCADE with foreign_keys enabled).

verdicts.rationale: Cascade test passes.

claims.statement: The GitHub API client bounds every outbound request with a 10 second timeout and rejects response bodies over 256 KiB and non-success statuses before decoding.

evidence.summary: reqwest client built with a 10s total timeout; read_bounded_body rejects non-success status first and returns Decode when body.len() > 262_144 before serde decode. However response.bytes().await buffers the full body BEFORE the length check, so the 256 KiB cap does not bound memory (only the 10s timeout does), contrary to the doc comment that larger payloads are not worth buffering.

evidence.locator: cargo test --lib github::client::tests (18 github tests pass); grep -n "262\|MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES\|timeout" src/github/client.rs tests
evidence.summary: No test serves a body over 256 KiB or a stalled server; the only decode tests use small malformed bodies. Neither the timeout nor the size limit is exercised by any test, though the claim requires test verification.

verdicts.rationale: Code sets a 10s timeout and a 256 KiB post-read rejection, but no test exercises either, and the body is fully buffered before the size check so the cap does not bound memory. Level 3 needs test evidence. Fix: stream the body with a 262144 byte limit (reject on exceeding) and add tests with a stalled server and a 300 KiB response asserting Transport and Decode errors.

claims.statement: The GitHub client never exposes credentials: the private key, JWT and installation token are zeroizing or redacted in Debug, error variants carry no body/URL/credential, and the module emits no logs containing them.

evidence.summary: Debug for GitHubAppClient and CachedInstallationToken prints [REDACTED]; JWT and token are Zeroizing<String>; config key is Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> with redacted Debug (test config.rs:1393); every map_err discards the underlying reqwest/jwt error (which could embed the URL); GitHubClientError variants are unit variants. The only logs (refresh.rs) print the unit-variant error and fixed outcome strings; no tracing call in client.rs. bearer_auth marks the header sensitive. Residual: response Bytes/Vec holding the minted token are not zeroized (memory hygiene only), and reqwest follows redirects by default (reqwest strips Authorization across origins).

verdicts.rationale: Debug redaction, Zeroizing wrappers, error variants without content and absence of credential logging were verified by reading all logging sites; residual non-zeroized response buffers are memory hygiene only.

claims.statement: App authentication signs an RS256 JWT with lifetime <= 10 minutes (backdated 60s), and caches the installation token, re-minting it when within 60s of expiry.

evidence.summary: JWT: Header RS256, iat = now-60, exp = iat+540 (= now+480s, under GitHub's 600s cap), iss = app id. installation_token() reuses cached token while now+60s < expires_at else mints and replaces it.

Pass: tokens expiring in 3600s are usable, 60s and -1s are not; a token 30s from expiry triggers a mint attempt (error Jwt or Transport). No test decodes a signed JWT to check alg/iat/exp because the repo holds no RSA key; the remint test accepts either error.

verdicts.rationale: JWT arithmetic gives 480s lifetime RS256; the renewal margin predicate is unit tested. JWT signing itself is not covered by a test (no key available).

claims.statement: A 404 from the required-status-checks endpoint is cached as a confident empty set, whereas transport, auth, rate-limit, 5xx and decode failures are not cached and leave the branch unknown.

evidence.summary: All pass: 404 yields an empty RequiredChecks that the store treats as a fresh confident answer; 401/403/429/500 map to bounded errors; decode failure is an error; on a Forbidden fetch nothing is cached. Transport-error non-caching is covered by the same early-return in refresh.rs:190-199.

verdicts.rationale: Client and refresher tests cover 404 as a confident empty answer and failures as uncached.

claims.statement: Required-check refresh never blocks the webhook path: requests go through a bounded (64) try_send queue that drops when full, and a burst for one fresh branch causes exactly one GitHub API read.

evidence.summary: request() is sync with try_send. Observation: failed fetches (rate limit, 403) are not negatively cached, so every subsequent webhook for that branch re-enqueues a GitHub call (and a token mint); the 64-slot queue and serial loop bound concurrency but not the sustained call rate during an outage.
Pass: handle.request uses try_send on a 64-slot channel, drops when full without blocking; five refreshes for one branch call the source once; run loop stops on cancellation or when handles drop.

verdicts.rationale: Tests demonstrate non-blocking drop on a full 64-slot queue and one API read per burst. Failure outcomes are not negatively cached (neutral note) but the claim does not require that.

claims.statement: The required-check cache treats entries older than the TTL as absent, caps stored sets at 100 names, re-sanitizes names on read, and limits check_names to 16384 characters in the schema.

evidence.summary: 17 matching tests pass covering TTL staleness, re-sanitization on read, 100-name cap and the bounded migration columns (check_names length <= 16384, branch 1..255).

verdicts.rationale: Cache store tests cover TTL, re-sanitization, cap and schema bounds.

claims.statement: A branch name taken from the webhook payload cannot change the request path beyond the single /repos/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection/required_status_checks resource (no dot-segment traversal, query or fragment injection).

evidence.summary: WorkflowBranch::sanitize only strips control chars and truncates to 255; it does not reject '.'/'..' segments. BRANCH_SEGMENT_ENCODE_SET leaves '/' and '.' literal, so a payload branch like 'main/../../../../orgs/x' is substituted into the URL and the url crate (used by reqwest) normalizes dot segments, changing the request to another API path with the installation token. The doc comment relies on Git forbidding '..', but nothing validates the payload (a repo owner who holds the webhook secret can sign any branch string). Impact is limited to a GET whose response is parsed only for checks/contexts names, but it is a path-traversal primitive. '?', '#', '%' are encoded so query/fragment injection is blocked.

verdicts.rationale: Branch sanitization does not reject dot segments and the encode set leaves '/' and '.' literal, so a signed payload branch such as main/../../../../orgs/x is normalized by the url crate into a different API path carrying the installation token. Query and fragment injection is blocked, traversal is not, and no test covers it. Fix: in WorkflowBranch handling for the API URL, reject (return no lookup) any branch with a '.' or '..' path segment, and add a client test asserting such a branch makes no request.

verdicts.rationale: Code compares fixed-length SHA-256 digests via subtle ct_eq; no variable-time comparison of token bytes exists.

claims.statement: Rename and rotation re-encrypt in a single transaction: a rename re-encrypts under the new canonical name, a conflicting rename leaves the stored ciphertext unchanged, and the old name can no longer decrypt.

evidence.summary: validated_endpoint parses with url::Url::parse and returns Invalid unless scheme is http or https; applied to generic, traces and logs endpoint variables (config.rs:507-511).

Cases 'not a URL' and 'ftp://collector.example' for OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT are rejected. Only the generic variable is exercised; the signal-specific endpoint variables share the same function but are not directly covered by a rejection test.

verdicts.rationale: Single validator function enforces http/https and parse success for all three endpoint variables; test exercises both rejection kinds.

claims.statement: Signal-specific OTLP endpoint, headers and timeout variables override the generic ones, and a generic OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT gets /v1/traces and /v1/logs appended per signal.

evidence.summary: Test sets generic endpoint/headers/timeout plus traces-specific endpoint, logs-specific headers and traces timeout; asserts trace endpoint https://traces.example/v1/traces, log endpoint https://collector.example/base/v1/logs (suffix appended), trace timeout 800ms vs log 1200ms, and signal-specific headers resolved. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Override test asserts endpoint suffixing, per-signal timeouts and headers.

claims.statement: Debug output of RuntimeConfig and TelemetryConfig redacts OTLP endpoints and header values.

evidence.summary: Debug rendering of config is asserted not to contain collector.example, credential values, Sentry host or DSN secret, and to contain [REDACTED]. Passed. Endpoint and header values are held in Zeroizing wrappers.

verdicts.rationale: Redaction test passes with sentinel endpoint and credential values.

claims.statement: Resource attributes contain service.name (default github-webhook-exporter), service.version, and k8s.pod.name / k8s.namespace.name only when set in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES; every other resource key is dropped.

evidence.summary: validated_resource_attributes keeps only keys k8s.pod.name and k8s.namespace.name (others are filtered out via filter_map returning None); telemetry_resource sets service.name (default github-webhook-exporter), service.version=CARGO_PKG_VERSION plus those two.

Fixture sets OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=k8s.pod.name=exporter-0,k8s.namespace.name=tests,forbidden=value; the decoded OTLP resource contains service.name, service.version, k8s.pod.name, k8s.namespace.name and not 'forbidden'. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Both the filter code and a decoded OTLP resource assertion show only the allowed keys.

claims.statement: Absence of an OTLP endpoint disables remote export while local structured stderr logging stays active.

evidence.summary: With no endpoint the runtime is disabled yet structured stderr lines are still written; with an unavailable endpoint stderr logging also remains. Both passed (part of 130 telemetry tests).
is_enabled() is false when no OTLP endpoint variable is set.

verdicts.rationale: Disabled-runtime tests show stderr logging with no export.

claims.statement: The admission boundary never lets pending records exceed the configured queue capacity, even under concurrent producers, and releasing a batch restores exactly its size of capacity.

evidence.summary: Sequential test shows capacity 3 admits exactly 3, rejects the 4th, and release(2) frees exactly 2 slots; the concurrent test releases 64 contenders against capacity 8 and checks the admitted count does not exceed capacity. Both passed.
try_admit uses a compare-exchange loop that increments pending only when pending < capacity; release uses saturating CAS so pending cannot underflow. No locks or waits on the producer path.

verdicts.rationale: Exact-capacity and 64-way concurrent tests pass, and the CAS loop enforces the bound.

claims.statement: A record offered to a full queue is rejected without blocking and counted as exactly one github_telemetry_dropped_records_total{signal,reason=queue_full}.

evidence.summary: With the exporter blocked and queue capacity filled, the test asserts runtime.pending_*_records()==QUEUE_CAPACITY, dropped_*_records()==expected_drops for both signals and checks the Prometheus exposition lines for the drop counters. Passed.

QueueFull path calls record_drop which increments the local counter once and observer.drop_record -> metrics.record_telemetry_drops(signal, reason, 1) before any reporting; BoundarySpanProcessor::on_end only forwards to the SDK when Admitted, so no blocking send occurs.

verdicts.rationale: Integration test checks pending, drops and exposition; code path increments exactly once without blocking.

claims.statement: After processor shutdown begins, new records are rejected and counted as reason=pipeline_closed, and pending records stranded after a shutdown timeout are also counted as pipeline_closed drops.

evidence.summary: Tests assert admissions after close() return PipelineClosed and are counted with that reason, that records stranded after timeout are counted as pipeline_closed drops, and that late export after finalization is suppressed so they are not double counted. All passed.

verdicts.rationale: Queue unit tests cover closed admission and stranded-slot accounting.

claims.statement: Queue-drop stderr diagnostics are limited to one report per signal/reason per 60 seconds, and the next permitted report carries the accumulated suppressed count; concurrent callers never exceed one report per interval.

evidence.summary: Tests with an injected monotonic clock show one report per category per interval under concurrent callers, exact suppressed counts on the next report, and independent categories. Passed.
REPORT_INTERVAL_MILLIS=60_000, DROP_CATEGORY_COUNT=4 (2 signals x 2 drop reasons); claim_report uses a CAS on the next deadline and swaps the suppressed counter into the report line (suppressed=N).

verdicts.rationale: Limiter code and clocked concurrent tests agree with the 60s per-category rule.

claims.statement: Every failed OTLP export attempt emits exactly one stderr diagnostic line and increments exactly one github_telemetry_export_failures_total series, with no rate limiting.

evidence.summary: Repeated export failures within the same instant each produce a line (no limiter), the SDK-level failure path increments each bounded series once, and an HTTP-classified failure is not double counted as internal. Passed.

export_failure_with_context increments the metric then write_failure unconditionally (no limiter); observe_export suppresses SDK-level recording when the HTTP layer already classified a failure (classified_failures sequence compare).

verdicts.rationale: Three reports for three failures and metric value 3 shown; no limiter on the failure path.

claims.statement: Exporter diagnostics are written through a dedicated stderr sink and not through tracing or the OpenTelemetry log API, so a failed log export cannot recursively create another OTLP log.

evidence.summary: The production sink StderrSink calls io::stderr().lock().write_all(line) on a line built with format! from literals/enums; the module imports no tracing macros or opentelemetry logs API. Failures are ignored via drop(sink.write(..)).
Outage tests with log export enabled complete without a recursion explosion and count each failure once; passed. Not a direct proof of non-recursion, but consistent with the static analysis.

After drops and failures occurred with log export active, the test asserts the captured OTLP logs do not contain the text 'telemetry pipeline diagnostic', directly demonstrating no recursive entry into the OTLP log pipeline. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Direct stderr sink plus a test asserting diagnostics never appear in captured OTLP logs.

claims.statement: Diagnostic lines contain only fixed literals, closed enum values, a three-digit status, a closed detail token, and integer counts; endpoint URLs, headers, response bodies and raw error text never appear.

evidence.summary: Unit test asserts the exact line format for status/detail; integration test with a collector returning a body asserts the body, configured endpoint and credentials are absent from stderr. Passed.

Lines are built only from signal.as_str(), reason.as_str(), numeric status, ExportFailureDetail::as_str() and integer suppressed; classify_reqwest_error uses is_timeout/status/is_connect/is_builder/is_redirect only, never Display/Debug.

verdicts.rationale: Exact-line unit test, response-body leak test and code inspection agree.

claims.statement: HTTP-client failures are classified from typed reqwest predicates into timeout, http_response (with status), transport (connect/request_builder/redirect/request detail), and malformed OTLP success bodies into encoding, without using Display or Debug text.

evidence.summary: Real local-socket failures classify to HttpResponse(503), Timeout, Transport+Connect, RequestBuilder, Request, Redirect, and a malformed 200 body to Encoding. All four passed.

verdicts.rationale: Real-socket classification tests pass for each category.

claims.statement: The production reqwest dependency enables rustls, and the production blocking client construction can attempt an HTTPS connection.

evidence.summary: reqwest = { version = \"0.13\", default-features = false, features = [\"blocking\", \"rustls\"] }.

Local non-TLS listener: the production build_blocking_http_client() issues an https:// request, the listener accepts a TCP connection (TLS handshake begins) and the request errors. Passed, no network access.

verdicts.rationale: Feature flag present and a local test shows the production client opens a connection for https.

claims.statement: A collector outage leaves the authenticated webhook response at 204 and /health/ready at 200, and the failure is counted.

evidence.summary: Readiness is 200 before, the signed webhook returns 204 during an unreachable-collector outage, readiness is 200 after, and failure counters rise. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Test asserts 204 and ready 200 before/after an outage plus counters.

claims.statement: A blocked (non-responding) collector does not delay the webhook response beyond a bounded time, and with full queues the pending count stays at capacity while drops are counted.

evidence.summary: With a blocked collector the response is wrapped in tokio::time::timeout(2s), returns 204, and readiness stays 200; the bounds test shows pending==capacity and drops counted. Both passed. Request-latency bound is a 2s test ceiling rather than a tight production bound.

verdicts.rationale: Blocked-collector tests pass with a bounded response and exact queue bounds.

claims.statement: Runtime shutdown starts trace and log provider shutdown concurrently under one shared deadline, and reports TimedOut rather than waiting past the deadline if one hangs.

evidence.summary: Tests show both providers' shutdown tasks begin before either is awaited, one hanging signal consumes only the single shared deadline and yields TimedOut, failures are reported once, and a second shutdown is idempotent. Passed.
End-to-end shutdown flushes accepted trace and log records to the mock OTLP receiver. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Shutdown tests prove concurrent start and single shared deadline; end-to-end flush test passes.

claims.statement: main always runs telemetry runtime shutdown with the configured OTEL shutdown timeout after the service returns, including when the service returns an error.

evidence.summary: run() stores service_result = run_service(..).await (not propagated with ?), then unconditionally logs and awaits spawn_blocking(telemetry_runtime.shutdown(telemetry_shutdown_timeout)) with the config's OTEL shutdown timeout, then returns service_result. Early failures inside run_service therefore still flush. Only the init error (before the runtime exists) skips shutdown, which is correct. No test executes main().

verdicts.rationale: Control flow in run() unconditionally calls shutdown after the service result is captured; analysis-only, no test runs main.

claims.statement: The primary span names are exactly http.request, github.webhook.authenticate, github.webhook.process, config.repository.write, sqlite.query and merge_queue.update, and the webhook hierarchy exports them nested.

evidence.summary: Operation::span constructs info_span! with literal names http.request, github.webhook.authenticate, github.webhook.process, config.repository.write, sqlite.query, merge_queue.update (plus retention.run, documented in build-spec as an extra).
In-process OTLP receiver tests decode exported spans and assert names and parent/child nesting (http.request root with authenticate/process/sqlite/merge_queue/config write children). Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Literal span names in trace.rs and OTLP receiver tests confirm names and nesting.

claims.statement: No span, log or resource carries webhook payload, secrets, signatures or authorization headers: sentinel secret values never appear in captured OTLP spans, logs or stderr.

evidence.summary: Tests inject sentinel secret, authorization header, actor, command, raw URL, raw reason and payload fragments, then scan captured OTLP spans, logs, stderr and Prometheus exposition and assert none appear. All passed.

All span attribute keys are compile-time constants (http method/route/status, ghe.* normalized enums, db.operation.name, github.* validated identifiers); no key for signature, authorization, body or raw URL exists. Webhook secrets are not reachable from the span helpers.

verdicts.rationale: Sentinel-scanning tests across spans, logs, stderr and metrics pass; attribute keys are a constant allowlist with no secret-bearing key.

claims.statement: As written in the OTLP spec, webhook spans never carry repository names, repository IDs, pull-request numbers, commit SHAs or delivery IDs.

evidence.summary: The github.webhook.process and merge_queue.update spans call set_repository_name, set_repository_id, set_delivery_id and set_commit_sha (trace.rs keys github.repository.name, github.repository.id, github.delivery.id, github.commit.sha, github.pull_request.number). This contradicts spec 04's forbidden list.

The test name and body deliberately assert these identifiers are present on spans (span-only), and docs/build-spec.md OpenTelemetry says authenticated webhook spans use the canonical repository name and a delivery ID may be in trace context. Later specs amended the policy; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-04-otlp-observability.md was not updated, so the document and code disagree.

verdicts.rationale: Webhook spans deliberately carry repository name, repository id, delivery id, commit SHA and PR number, which spec 04 lists as forbidden. Later specs and docs/build-spec.md changed the policy, so the code is consistent with current intent but the spec text is stale. Fix: edit the Spans section of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-04-otlp-observability.md so the forbidden list matches the span-only identifier policy that src/telemetry/trace.rs and docs/build-spec.md implement.

claims.statement: The HTTP client used for OTLP export does not forward configured credential headers (for example x-api-key) to a different host when the collector answers with a redirect.

evidence.summary: The client is built with reqwest::blocking::Client::builder().timeout(..).build() and no redirect(Policy::none()), so reqwest's default Policy::limited(10) applies (reqwest-0.13.4/src/redirect.rs:160-164).

On a cross-host redirect reqwest strips only authorization, cookie, cookie2, proxy-authorization and www-authenticate. Operator-configured OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS such as x-api-key (see config.rs test with x-api-key) are retained and forwarded to the redirect target. Only the redirect-failure classification is tested (http_client.rs:258), not header forwarding.

verdicts.rationale: The OTLP reqwest client uses the default follow-up-to-10-redirects policy, and reqwest strips only standard auth headers on cross-host redirects, so custom headers such as x-api-key would be sent to whatever host a redirecting collector names. Fix: call .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none()) in build_blocking_http_client in src/telemetry.rs and add a local test that a 307 to a second listener receives no x-api-key header.

claims.statement: GHE_WORKFLOW_JOB_MAX_STEPS defaults to 256, accepts 1 through 1024, and rejects 0, 1025, non-numeric, overflowing and non-Unicode values with an error naming only the variable.

evidence.summary: Default is 256, 1 accepted, 1024 accepted; 0, not-a-number, 1025 and 18446744073709551616 rejected; non-Unicode rejected with message 'environment variable GHE_WORKFLOW_JOB_MAX_STEPS has an invalid value' that does not disclose the value. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Config tests cover default, boundaries 1 and 1024, rejects 0/1025/non-numeric/overflow/non-Unicode.

claims.statement: A completed workflow job with exactly the configured number of steps exports a complete job trace, while a job above the limit exports no job or step span and the delivery still gets the authenticated 204.

evidence.summary: Branch is step_count > step_limit (strictly greater), so the limit is inclusive; over-limit path only records the rejection and does not call project_completed_job or the emitter.
At-limit job exports a complete trace; the over-limit test (limit 2, 3 steps) gets 204, a durable delivery claim, and zero workflow task spans for that delivery. Both passed.

verdicts.rationale: Boundary tests and strict greater-than comparison show inclusive limit and no spans when over.

claims.statement: Step counting in admission consumes each step as IgnoredAny and retains only validated positive run ID, attempt, job ID and the count; non-array steps or non-positive identifiers yield no admission.

evidence.locator: cargo test api::workflow (admission_counts_steps_and_validates_identifiers, admission_missing_steps_defaults_to_zero, admission_rejects_malformed_json_bytes, non-array steps cases; src/api/workflow_job.rs:517-620)
evidence.summary: Admission counts steps (including a large array), defaults missing steps to 0, and returns None for malformed JSON, non-positive IDs and non-array steps. 32 api::workflow tests passed.
StepCount's Visitor consumes each element as IgnoredAny with checked_add; WorkflowJobAdmission stores only three validated IDs and usize step_count, and its Debug redacts IDs.

verdicts.rationale: Visitor discards elements and admission struct retains only IDs and count; unit tests cover invalid inputs.

claims.statement: Each over-limit job increments github_workflow_job_trace_rejections_total{reason=too_many_steps} exactly once, observes github_workflow_job_steps, and a duplicate delivery does neither a second time.

evidence.summary: First test asserts histogram count 1/sum 3 and rejections_total{reason=too_many_steps}==1; the duplicate test redelivers the same over-limit delivery and asserts the counters remain at one observation/one rejection. Both passed.

Histogram buckets are 0,5,10,20,40,64,128,256,512,1024; rejection reason is a closed enum seeded at startup; observation and rejection happen only after DeliveryClaim::New (the Duplicate arm returns before).

verdicts.rationale: Metric lines asserted for first delivery and unchanged on duplicate; claim ordering in code confirms.

claims.statement: The too_many_steps warning carries only reason, repository, run ID, attempt, job ID, delivery ID, step_count and step_limit, and excludes names, SHAs, actors, commands, output, URLs and payload fragments.

evidence.summary: Asserts the exported OTLP rejection log has exactly the attribute keys delivery_id, reason, repository_name, step_count, step_limit, workflow_job_id, workflow_run_attempt, workflow_run_id, no trace/span context, and that sentinels for workflow/job/step names, SHA, PR, actor, command, output, logs, URLs, payload fragment, signature, authorization, secrets and collector details appear in neither stderr, logs nor exposition. Passed.

warn! carries exactly reason, repository_name, workflow_run_id, workflow_run_attempt, workflow_job_id, delivery_id, step_count, step_limit with a fixed message, emitted with parent: None under an empty context.

verdicts.rationale: Test asserts the exact attribute key set and absence of every forbidden sentinel.

claims.statement: An accepted completed workflow job exports one independent root span github.workflow.job with a direct github.workflow.step child per reported step, in order, with historical timestamps.

evidence.summary: Captured OTLP spans show one github.workflow.job root with no parent and independent trace ID from the request, one github.workflow.step child per step in order with historical start/end timestamps. Passed.
emit() builds the root with an empty Context::new() and with_start_time; each step is built against the root's context and finished with end_with_timestamp, in job.steps() order.

verdicts.rationale: OTLP-captured spans and emitter code show independent root and ordered direct step children with historical times.

claims.statement: Display names exported in workflow spans have all Unicode control characters removed and are truncated to 128 characters; unrecognised conclusions are exported only as the normalized closed vocabulary.

evidence.summary: Unit test checks control-character stripping and the 128-character cap (src/telemetry/workflow.rs:117-140 uses char::is_control and MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH=128); conclusion normalization is a closed enum and unknown inputs export as 'other'. Passed. Note char::is_control covers Unicode Cc only, not format characters such as bidi overrides.

verdicts.rationale: Sanitizer test and closed conclusion enum support the claim as written (control = Unicode Cc).

claims.statement: Span status maps success to Ok, failure and timed_out to Error with the fixed description workflow_failed, and cancelled, skipped, neutral and other to Unset.

evidence.summary: Status mapping verified in unit and OTLP tests; src/telemetry/workflow.rs:1012-1018 maps Success->Ok, Failure/TimedOut->Status::error(\"workflow_failed\"), the rest->Unset. Passed. Exception: a failed job confidently known not to be a required check has its root status suppressed to Unset (workflow.rs:369-375), a separate documented rule.

verdicts.rationale: Mapping function and tests match the spec's status table.

claims.statement: Each failed or timed-out step span gets one exception span event with type GitHubActionsTaskFailure or GitHubActionsTaskTimeout and a bounded 'CI task failed/timed out: <task>' message, and the job span gets one only when no failed or timed-out child step explains it.

evidence.summary: Tests assert exception events with name 'exception', type GitHubActionsTaskFailure/Timeout, message 'CI task failed: cargo test' / 'CI task timed out: ...' at the historical end time, no event for non-failures, and the job fallback only when no failing step exists. Passed.

Step loop adds the event only when conclusion.emits_synthetic_error() and sets child_error_emitted; the job fallback is guarded by !child_error_emitted; event attributes are exactly exception.type and exception.message (no stacktrace/escaped).

verdicts.rationale: Unit tests and emitter control flow show per-step events and guarded job fallback with fixed attributes.

claims.statement: The pipeline-run root trace ID is the first 16 bytes of sha256('gha-pipeline:{repository}:{run_id}:{run_attempt}') using the canonical lowercase repository, with all-zero digests falling back to a random ID; the published fixture values match an independent recomputation.
claims.source: 2026-08-12-workflow-span-context plan; changelog on deterministic pipeline trace IDs (pointer only)

evidence.summary: Independent recomputation gives 744f46e18e520d0324ebe726e54e6861, equal to the Rust test fixture and to book/src/reference/traces.md:240. Code builds the preimage '{domain}:{repo}:{run_id}:{attempt}', takes digest[..16], and addressable_trace_id returns None for all-zero.

Fixture test pins both published vectors (owner/repository:31:2 and stackblitz/bolt:12345678901:1); the zero-prefix guard test confirms None for zero bytes and Some for a single bit. Passed. Random-ID fallback (pipeline_root_context returning an empty Context) is by inspection only because the all-zero digest is unreachable.

verdicts.rationale: Independent SHA-256 recomputation matches the code fixture and the published docs value.

claims.statement: The derived pipeline trace ID differs across repositories, runs and attempts, is stable across re-emission and repository-name casing/padding, and the exported root keeps that trace ID without a parent span.

evidence.summary: Tests assert distinct IDs for different repo/run/attempt, equality for re-emission and for ' Owner/Repository ' vs canonical, root span_context.trace_id equals the derived value, is not INVALID, and the root has no parent. All passed.
Webhook-level test exports the pipeline trace with links to each job trace. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Separation, stability, normalization and root-without-parent properties are each asserted by passing tests.

claims.statement: A completed run with more than 256 linked jobs emits no pipeline trace, increments rejections{reason=too_many_jobs} and logs a bounded warning; a run with no linked jobs emits nothing.

evidence.summary: Over-limit run: warning log with reason too_many_jobs, repository and delivery attributes, rejection metric lines, and no seeded job span exported; run with no linked jobs exports nothing. Passed. MAX_PIPELINE_JOB_SPANS=256 at pipeline.rs:40.

verdicts.rationale: Integration test asserts rejection warning, metric and absence of pipeline trace.

claims.statement: The workflow_run_contexts and workflow_job_links stores are keyed by repository, run, attempt (and job) with upsert semantics and prune at most 1,000 rows per call by update time.

evidence.summary: Tests insert more than 1,000 expired rows and show one prune call deletes at most 1,000 by update time; attempts are independent; same job recorded twice is replaced; listing is scoped by run/attempt and limit. 20 storage tests passed. SQL uses ON CONFLICT(repository_id, run, attempt[, job]) upserts (workflow_run_store.rs:58, workflow_job_link_store.rs:91).
Migration tests confirm the tables carry only bounded identifier/branch/event columns. Passed.

verdicts.rationale: Store tests and SQL show upsert keys, scoping and 1,000-row prune bound.
